rationale: Lycopolitan reflex of ϩⲁⲙⲟⲓ̈ 'O that, would that' (wish-particle). Standard Lyc. ⲍ-for-ϩ. Used by Aurades to introduce his petition to Mani.
Lycopolitan idiom ⲁ-ⲣⲉⲛ-ⲧϥ̄ '(this is) his name' — used after a proper name to specify identity. Standard Coptic name-introduction formula in dialectal form.

Greek loanword κάπηλος 'small trader, retailer.' Aurades is identified as 'son of the merchant' — fitting the social register of Mani's early disciples. Distinct from ⲉϣⲱⲧ (in glossary as 'merchant' for ⲙⲛⲧⲓⲉⲡϣⲱⲧ).
Lycopolitan ⲡⲉⲛ-ⲭⲁⲓⲥ 'our Lord' — first-person plural possessive form of ⲡⲁⲭⲁⲓⲥ (in glossary). Standard disciples' address to Mani.
Lycopolitan ⲡⲉⲛ-ⲫⲱⲥⲧⲏⲣ 'our Illuminator' — first-person plural possessive form of ⲡⲫⲱⲥⲧⲏⲣ (in glossary). Standard disciples' address to Mani as φωστήρ.
Lycopolitan ⲡⲉϫⲁϥ 'he said' with -ϩ suffix (= ⲛⲁϥ 'to him' fused), giving 'he said to him.' Variant of accumulated ⲡⲁⲭⲉⲩ 'he said (to him).' Possessive-dative speech-introducer.
Lycopolitan interrogative ⲛ̄ⲁϣ ⲛ̄ϩⲉ 'in what manner.' Standard Coptic question-formula introducing inquiries about the manner of an event.
